The cross sections were computed using the Tai formulas, with corrections to the original formulas.
Results are presented for both vertically and horizontally polarized radars.
Cross sections are given for 2l/λ ratios between 0.16 and 0.55, in 5° elevation angle increments.
Table I presents the dipole cross-section σ(θ)/λ^2, where the subscripts vv and hh denote the radar polarization.
Table II extends the information in Table I, providing cross sections for A values of 40, 60, 100, 200, 400, 600, 1000, 2000, and 4000.
Table III gives the cross sections assuming a random orientation distribution of the dipoles.
The measured-to-computed response ratio has an average value of -1.5 dB ± 1 dB in the range 0.19 ≤ 2l/λ ≤ 0.37.
For dipoles with 2l/λ = 0.5 (approximately 2 inches long), the measured-to-computed response ratio is -4.0 dB.
The random orientation distribution failed to give a correct polarization response ratio at all values of 2l/λ and θ tested.
The average of the vertical and horizontal measured-to-computed ratios for 2l/λ = 0.5 under the random orientation assumption is -1.8 dB.
The measured vertical response is approximately 1 dB lower than the random-distribution computed response for 2l/λ = 0.5.
The measured horizontal response is lower than the computed response by 3 dB for 2l/λ = 0.5.
Dipoles less than 3 inches long should use the horizontal-vertical distribution, while longer dipoles shift towards the random orientation.
The improved accuracy from the horizontal-vertical distribution corresponds to a 40% reduction in the weight of chaff needed to produce a given echo.
The tables provide results 1.5 dB closer to the measured values than the Van Vleck method.
